title: A Taxonomy of Rater Disagreements: Surveying Challenges & Opportunities from the Perspective of Annotating Online Toxicity

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying existing literature to construct a comprehensive taxonomy of reasons for inter-rater disagreements, mapping out how rater heterogeneity, subjective opinions, and individual beliefs impact toxicity annotations.

Reviewing prior studies to evaluate how variations in raters' cultural backgrounds and regional norms (e.g., differences between Western and Eastern environments) influence their subjective interpretation of toxicity triggers.

Summarizing research that identifies a rater's racial identity as a moderating factor in toxicity annotation, and discussing bias alleviation mechanisms used to mitigate racial bias in training datasets.

Evaluating literature on how a rater's first language, overall language proficiency, and exposure to multilingual code-switching or neologisms affect their accuracy and agreement in classifying toxic behavior.
Citing empirical studies that demonstrate how demographic factors, specifically a rater's age, exert a substantial influence on the subjective labeling of hate speech.
